Developer comments: All examples show batch processing - loading a complete dataset computing statistics done. No mention of streaming
None of these libraries are designed for streaming data. They all assume you have the complete dataset in memory. This is a major limitation
In modern data infrastructure: Data arrives continuously Datasets too large to fit in memory Need real-time statistics Can't wait hours for batch jobs

With batch DP: Collect all data compute statistic add noise once. With streaming DP: Data arrives incrementally want to query at any time need appropriate noise. These are fundamentally different! Current libraries only support batch
Every query consumes epsilon. If I query 1000 times I've consumed epsilon=100! With batch DP I add noise once. With this streaming approach I add noise per query. This fundamentally doesn't work
If I add noise to 1 million events the accumulated noise is massive! For 1M events: True count ~7841 Noise std: 1M. The noise completely overwhelms the signal. Useless results

Under continual observation can query multiple times but privacy guarantee is across all queries. This requires algorithms like binary mechanism honaker mechanism. But these don't exist in current libraries
Pan-privacy protects even if internal state is leaked. Pan-privacy is essential for streaming where internal state might be exposed. But no pan-private algorithms exist
More recent data has stronger privacy guarantees. Useful when recent user data needs more protection. But no time-decayed algorithms exist
